title: Active learning identifies a higher-activity streptavidin variant for gold-catalyzed hydroamination
summary: An iterative active-learning campaign engineered a streptavidin artificial metalloenzyme for the known-to-the-authors gold-catalyzed hydroamination of 2-ethynylaniline to indole. Gaussian-process models guided screening across five residues in a 3.2-million-variant sequence space. The final-round library contained 38% variants more active than the prior reference, compared with 3% in the initial library. The leading variant, Sav CTNLV, showed 18-fold higher cell-specific activity than wild-type Sav and threefold higher activity than the previous reference variant in replicate testing.
ai_technology: Active-learning Gaussian-process regression model with optimized sequence descriptors and experimental-noise estimates
organization: ETH Zurich; University of Basel and University of Regensburg

evidence.tested: The leading variant, Sav CTNLV, showed 18-fold higher cell-specific activity than wild-type Sav and threefold higher activity than the previous reference variant in replicate testing.
evidence.unknown: The hydroamination reaction and streptavidin–gold artificial metalloenzyme were established in earlier work by the same group; this record is specifically the later AI-guided identification of a higher-activity five-residue variant, not discovery of a new reaction. Activity was measured in an E. coli periplasmic whole-cell assay; purified variants did not retain the same rank order in vitro. Industrial utility or catalytic scale-up was not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The model used measured sequence-activity data from thousands of variants to select exploratory and exploitation libraries across five residues, then prioritized variants for experimental testing. It enabled identification of a high-activity sequence in a large combinatorial space; the paper reports considering experimental uncertainty in its rankings.
